description: VMAF (Video Multi-method Assessment Fusion) decomposed. Developed by Netflix in 2016, VMAF is a full-reference perceptual quality metric that fuses three elementary metrics — VIF (Visual Information Fidelity), DLM (Detail Loss Metric), and TI (motion-based Temporal Information) — via a support-vector regressor trained on subjective scores. The trained model maps from elementary feature scores to a 0-100 quality estimate that correlates ~0.93 with viewer mean opinion scores.

sub_mechanisms.name: VIF_visual_information_fidelity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Computes the mutual information shared between source and reconstructed image at each scale of a steerable pyramid decomposition, normalised by source self-information. Score: ratio of preserved information to total source information.
sub_mechanisms.why: Information-theoretic basis: distortion that destroys image information is more harmful than distortion that just shifts pixel values. VIF captures this — blurring (information loss) hurts more than slight shifts (no info loss). Works well for compression artifacts where information is genuinely destroyed by quantisation.

sub_mechanisms.name: DLM_detail_loss_metric
sub_mechanisms.definition: Decomposes both source and reconstructed images into 'additive impairment' (smooth distortion like blur) and 'subtractive impairment' (detail loss like edge degradation). DLM measures the subtractive component.
sub_mechanisms.why: Blurring and detail loss are perceptually different. DLM separates them so the regressor can weight them differently. Detail loss is often more annoying than smooth blur — DLM lets VMAF capture this asymmetry.

sub_mechanisms.name: TI_temporal_information
sub_mechanisms.definition: Captures the temporal complexity of the source: the average magnitude of frame-to-frame difference. Used to weight other features (high-motion content hides spatial artifacts).
sub_mechanisms.why: Viewer attention is captured by motion; spatial artifacts in fast-moving regions are less noticed than in still ones. TI provides the regressor with content-difficulty context, letting it scale the other features' importance per scene.

sub_mechanisms.name: multi_scale_decomposition
sub_mechanisms.definition: VIF is computed at multiple spatial scales (typically 4 octaves). Each scale captures different artifact frequencies.
sub_mechanisms.why: Multi-scale matches the HVS's multi-resolution processing. Low-scale captures coarse blur; high-scale captures fine-detail loss. Per-scale scores feed the regressor independently.

sub_mechanisms.name: support_vector_regressor
sub_mechanisms.definition: VMAF's fusion stage: an SVR trained on subjective MOS scores from public databases (NFLX-Public, VQEG-HD, etc.). Input: per-frame VIF + DLM + TI feature vectors. Output: 0-100 quality.
sub_mechanisms.why: The relationship between elementary features and viewer scores is non-linear and content-dependent. SVR learns the mapping from data, capturing what no closed-form combination would. The model file (a few KB) is the difference between 'features' and 'quality estimate'.

sub_mechanisms.name: pooling_method
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-frame VMAF scores are pooled into a single video-level score via mean, harmonic mean, or percentile (the spec uses arithmetic mean by default).
sub_mechanisms.why: Different pooling methods correlate differently with viewer ratings. Harmonic mean emphasises worst frames (typical artifacts); arithmetic mean averages. Choice depends on application — Netflix uses harmonic for streaming QoE because viewers remember the worst moments.

sub_mechanisms.name: phone_model_variant
sub_mechanisms.definition: VMAF-NEG (no enhancement gain): a variant that doesn't reward super-resolution/enhancement above the source. Used when output quality should be source-fidelity, not 'looks better than source'.
sub_mechanisms.why: Some encoders apply mild sharpening that can score higher than the reference on VMAF. NEG variants penalise this, ensuring VMAF measures FIDELITY rather than enhancement.

sub_mechanisms.name: subjective_score_training_set
sub_mechanisms.definition: VMAF's regressor is trained on databases of (source, distorted, MOS) triples — typically ~1000 video pairs with viewer ratings.
sub_mechanisms.why: The model is only as good as its training data. Netflix's NFLX-Public set is biased toward streaming content; VMAF is most accurate for that. Off-corpus content (animation, screen capture) gets less reliable scores.

sub_mechanisms.name: VMAF_4K_variant
sub_mechanisms.definition: VMAF-4K is trained on 4K subjective data and tuned for that resolution. Generic VMAF can be applied to 4K but the 4K variant is more accurate for that case.
sub_mechanisms.why: Viewer perception scales non-linearly with resolution; a model trained at 1080p doesn't transfer perfectly to 4K. Per-resolution variants capture the resolution-specific quality functions.

sub_mechanisms.name: open_source_implementation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Netflix released libvmaf as open source in 2016, with reference implementation and model files. Available on every major platform.
sub_mechanisms.why: Open-source release is what made VMAF the industry default. Closed perceptual metrics (e.g., proprietary PSY-OPT in some encoders) couldn't be cross-compared; open VMAF let competitive ABR ladders be designed with a common metric.

derivation_rules.name: metric_fusion_via_regression_beats_closed_form
if: multiple elementary metrics each capture part of perceptual quality
then: a regressor trained on subjective scores fuses them more accurately than a hand-tuned combination
derivation_rules.why: Hand-tuned weights are guesses; the data-driven SVR learns the optimal combination. VMAF's correlation with MOS (~0.93) is significantly higher than any single-metric or hand-weighted-combination approach.

derivation_rules.name: information_theoretic_basis_predicts_quality
if: a distortion destroys source information (vs just shifting it)
then: VIF predicts this is perceptually worse
derivation_rules.why: Compression artifacts genuinely destroy information through quantisation. VIF's information-theoretic framework correctly identifies blur and detail loss as more harmful than dithering or noise. This is why VMAF outperforms PSNR — PSNR doesn't distinguish information loss from value shift.

derivation_rules.name: temporal_information_modulates_spatial_quality
then: spatial artifacts are perceptually less impactful
derivation_rules.why: Viewer attention is captured by motion; static spatial artifacts in fast-moving regions go unnoticed. TI lets VMAF reduce spatial-feature weights for high-motion content, matching viewer judgments.

derivation_rules.name: open_source_enables_industry_default
if: a perceptual metric is open source with public model files
then: it becomes the industry default for streaming QoE
derivation_rules.why: ABR ladder optimisation requires a shared metric across encoders, CDNs, and decoders. Open VMAF made this possible — every party in the streaming pipeline can compute it. Proprietary metrics fragment the industry.

derivation_rules.name: training_data_determines_generalisation_quality
if: a metric's regressor is trained on a particular content distribution
then: accuracy on that distribution is high; off-distribution is lower
derivation_rules.why: Streaming content (Netflix's training corpus) is well-covered. Animation, screen capture, low-fps content are less well-covered. Per-domain variants (VMAF-4K, VMAF-NEG) address this within their scope.
